title: Existence of the chromatic polynomial
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex set, and write $n$ for the number of its vertices and $\pi_k(G)$ for the number of distinct proper $k$-colourings of $G$. Then there is a polynomial $p \in \bbz[x]$ with integer coefficients such that $p(k) = \pi_k(G)$ for every $k \in \bbn$; moreover $p$ has degree $n$, leading coefficient $1$, and constant term $0$, and its coefficients alternate in sign, in the sense that $(-1)^{n-i}\,a_i \ge 0$ for every $i$, where $a_i$ denotes the coefficient of $x^i$ in $p$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph (Fintype V)
the vertex set is nonempty (Nonempty V)
